items.q: A 48-year-old man with chronic severe alcohol dependence is brought to the emergency department with confusion, horizontal nystagmus, and truncal ataxia. Administration of intravenous glucose without prior thiamine administration risks precipitating acute lactic acidosis and neurological worsening due to impairment of which enzyme complex?
items.exp: The pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase require thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP, vitamin B1) as an essential cofactor. In thiamine deficiency, glucose loading drives glycolysis but pyruvate cannot enter the TCA cycle via PDH, accumulating and converting into lactic acid, which precipitates severe lactic acidosis and Wernicke encephalopathy.
r: Incorrect. PFK-1 does not require thiamine pyrophosphate.
Correct. Pyruvate dehydrogenase requires thiamine pyrophosphate; glucose without thiamine worsens Wernicke encephalopathy.
Incorrect. Citrate synthase does not require thiamine.
Incorrect. Lactate dehydrogenase uses NADH, not thiamine.
items.kp: Pyruvate dehydrogenase requires thiamine pyrophosphate; administering glucose without thiamine precipitates acute Wernicke encephalopathy.
